entries.topic: What to keep ready before a warning
entries.content: Keep in one bag: drinking water, dry food, any regular medicines, a torch with spare cells, a power bank, and photocopies of identity documents in a plastic cover.
Move to the highest floor or higher ground before water rises, not during. Do not walk or drive through moving water. Switch off the mains supply at the board before leaving if it is safe to reach.
Stay indoors away from windows. Do not go outside during the calm of the eye; the wind returns from the opposite direction. Move to the designated cyclone shelter if told to by officials.
The all-in-one emergency number in India is 112. NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) helpline is 011-24363260. The Indian Coast Guard number is 1554.

entries.topic: About the alerts shown in this app
entries.content: The hazard alerts displayed in the Sahayak prototype are sample data for demonstration and are not live warnings. Real warnings come from IMD and the state disaster management authority.

Stay indoors between 12 noon and 3 pm. Drink water often even when not thirsty. Wear light, loose cotton clothing and cover your head outdoors. Watch for dizziness, headache and a stopped sweat — those need medical help at once.

Treat all flood-contaminated water as unsafe. Boil water for at least one minute at a rolling boil before drinking, or use chlorine tablets as directed on the packet. Do not use flood water for washing food or utensils.
Official warnings for India come from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the state disaster management authority. The alerts displayed in this prototype are sample data, not live warnings.
